description: WIRE_FORMAT.md §5 'Row payloads', the two encode refusals (Phase 1960). A row feed's two hazards exist only on the way OUT: a host value no JSON document can carry is what an encoder either refuses or corrupts. So each vector is a row feed written in host-neutral CELL DESCRIPTORS, and its outcome: either the canonical bytes the feed encodes to, or the refusal, with its code and the cell it names (the row's zero-based position in the feed, and the key). A host maps each descriptor onto the native value its authoring surface uses for it and runs the row-feed encoder its node encode actually takes. A descriptor its authoring surface cannot hold (an `unspecified` dateTime on a host whose only date value is an instant) is UNREPRESENTABLE there: the host names each such vector, with the reason, in its own test, and fails when it skips one it did not name. This manifest is HAND-AUTHORED; no host emits it.

cellDescriptors.int64: a 64-bit signed integer, its decimal text in `value`. The integer TYPE matters, not the number: a double holding the same value is a float cell and is never refused.
cellDescriptors.dateTime: a date-time without an offset, ISO-8601 text in `value`, and `kind`: `utc` (the value names the UTC instant) or `unspecified` (the value names no instant: a .NET DateTime of Unspecified kind, a Python naive datetime).

codes.ROW_CELL_INEXACT_INTEGER: an int64 cell outside +/-2^53. Every integer in that range is exactly a double, so its bytes are exact; past it, the double an encoder would widen to is a different number.
codes.ROW_CELL_UNSPECIFIED_DATETIME: a date-time cell that names no instant. Converting it to Unix seconds would read the encoding machine's time zone, so one value would encode to different seconds on two machines.

vectors.description: the largest int64 every double holds exactly is admitted, in integer form (rule 5)
the negative bound is admitted too: the range is symmetric
one past the bound is refused, naming the cell; the retired encoder wrote 9007199254740992, a different number. The first row is clean, so the row position is read rather than assumed
one past the negative bound is refused the same way
a date-time naming its UTC instant encodes as Unix seconds, on every machine
the same wall-clock value naming no instant is refused, naming the cell; the retired encoder read the machine's time zone to pick the seconds
